topics.label: Introduction to the lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes students and introduces the lecture's focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Pathogen recognition through PAMPs and DAMPs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how the innate immune system identifies infections and cellular damage by sensing conserved molecular patterns while distinguishing self from non-self.

topics.label: Toll-like receptors and PRR cellular localization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genetic encoding, spatial distribution, and signaling cascades of membrane-associated pattern recognition receptors, focusing on Toll-like receptors.

topics.label: Cytoplasmic sensors and inflammasome activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine intracellular pattern recognition receptors and the multi-protein inflammasome pathway that processes mature inflammatory cytokines.

topics.label: Cellular dynamics and physiological effects of acute inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover how innate sentinel cells coordinate leukocyte trafficking and systemic signaling during an inflammatory response, along with the risks of pathological overactivation.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic persistence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the mechanisms that terminate inflammation, promote tissue repair, and manage unresolved threats through chronic inflammation and granuloma containment.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture and previews the next lecture on complements.
